scope: Opt-in modern-generation writer feasibility and bounded source-edit qualification; no public native creation/save API or general producer/fidelity qualification.

observations.repair: Unassessed: successful COM operations do not expose native repair; UI capture was unavailable.

reproduction: Build the opt-in probe with the pinned SDK, run the recorded create command with the repository image, then Invoke-NativePublisherOperation.ps1 -Operation Validate -Stage Full on an isolated copy. Compare native inventories and both PDFs against the explicit candidate expectations. Native artifact hashes identify this observed run; a subsequent native save can include different metadata.

sourceEditing.scope: Bounded modern-generation source edits: single-paragraph text/size/bold specimens below, with separate placement/paint, native text mutation, multi-paragraph and preview-invalidation qualification records.
limits: Repair-free opening remains unassessed.
Opaque record semantics and broad native-layout fidelity remain unassessed. Known SummaryInformation thumbnail invalidation is qualified separately; other cached records remain unassessed.
The 20-point request renders at 20.04 points in these native PDFs, within the recorded tolerance.
Original controls and native-resaved derivatives retain their distinct provenance.
Native whole-range text mutation is qualified separately on one styled candidate; it does not qualify all source-edit specimens.

placementAndPaint.scope: Nine bounded OfficeArt source edits; native inventory, PDF geometry/paint/image pixels, and save/reopen qualification.
limits: Only the listed objects and operations are qualified; native repair remains unassessed.
Original Contents AA/AB extents stay unchanged in the two qualified picture edits. Their general semantics remain unassessed.
Paired-master local bounds and physical composition are separate observations; no general layout-fidelity claim.

nativeTextMutation.scope: Whole-range text replacement through the native object model on the single physical unlinked text box in the styled candidate.
limits: One controlled whole-range replacement, not character-level or manual UI editing.
Immediate assigned text omits the final paragraph CR; save/reopen materializes it.
Native repair and general editing/formatting remain unassessed.
nativeTextMutation.runnerSourceHashScope: sha256 identifies executed worktree bytes; gitBlobSha256 identifies the Git-normalized file at runnerCommit.

paragraphEditing.scope: Bounded single-story/frame writing with unchanged paragraph topology, one character and paragraph formatting page, size/bold edits and source OPL preservation.
paragraphEditing.sourceHashScope: sha256 identifies qualified worktree bytes; gitBlobSha256 identifies Git-normalized files at codecCommit.
limits: Only the listed specimens and observed modern single-story profile are natively qualified.
Paragraph count/order and paragraph attributes remain unchanged. Multiple stories/format pages and other formatting remain unavailable.
Making a paragraph empty refuses output when its original CR OPL differs from the last visible run OPL.
Original OPLs, unrelated streams and directory metadata are retained; this does not qualify their opaque semantics or cached preview freshness.
Repair-free opening, general native layout and native typing defaults remain unassessed.

previewInvalidation.scope: Accepted native source content edits remove only the optional SummaryInformation thumbnail; unchanged source/no-op copies remain exact.
previewInvalidation.sourceHashScope: sha256 identifies qualified worktree bytes; gitBlobSha256 identifies Git-normalized files at codecCommit.
limits: Only the four exact post-invalidation specimens are natively qualified here; earlier qualification records identify their distinct pre-invalidation bytes and codec commits.
OfficeIMO removes the stale thumbnail without generating a replacement. Native resave recreates it in these cases; raw property hashes do not qualify thumbnail appearance.
Malformed SummaryInformation property-set structure refuses edits; unsupported semantic changes still refuse output.
Repair-free opening, general layout and other opaque/cached-record semantics remain unassessed.
